*GE description:*

When the system generates a reconnection invoice - either via Request for Disconnection execution or by using the Charge Fee button, and the same customer has unpaid overdue liabilities under two contracts associated with the same POD, the system should generate the reconnection invoice (and its corresponding liability) using the newest contract and its billing group.

The newest contract is defined as the contract with the later POD activation date, specifically for the POD that has the overdue liability.

This logic is not limited to re-signing cases. It applies to any scenario where one POD is tied to two contracts and both contracts have overdue liabilities for the same customer. In such cases, the reconnection invoice and its corresponding liability must always be generated using the contract with the later POD activation date and that contract’s billing group.

As I understand it, it’s not only about re-signing. When a POD is linked to two different contracts and has overdue liabilities under both, the reconnection invoice should use the newest contract and the newest billing group, correct? Also should we determine which is newer based on the contract creation date or the liability creation date?
the answer on the first question is yes. the second question needs to be discussed with dobromir.
For the second question, the newest contract is the last one in which the POD/PODs are currently active or were active (if the POD is deactivated and is not activated in a new contract).
For the first question, yes, provided that the customer remains the same.
If two contracts had this POD and the POD has already been deactivated in both contracts, are we looking at the contract in which the POD was activated later?
which one? The POD under one contract can be activated later but deactivated earlier than the POD under another contract.

Also, based on what i’ve checked so far (but we’ll verify it once more), the disconnection request has two liability columns: liabilities in the billing group and liabilities in the point of delivery (POD). One is at the billing-group level, while the other is at the POD level.

Currently, the reconnection invoice looks first at the liabilities in the POD and takes the latest liability contract from there. So, based on the changed logic, should it now look at both columns and select the newest contract liability across them?
One POD can’t be active in 2 contracts at the same time.
right, clear, so we are looking at later activation date and not creation date.
Please check the example from the issue. Here, the liabilities in the point of delivery are from the old contract, while the liabilities in the billing group are from the new contract.

Yes, but the general current logic is that in Liabilities in Billing Group, the liability generated per billing group is displayed, while in Liabilities in Point of Delivery, the liabilities generated per POD are displayed (when the separate checkbox is selected in Billing Group).

So, right now, it first checks Liabilities in Point of Delivery and takes the newest liability contract from there. With the new logic, it should instead choose the newest liability contract across both Liabilities in Billing Group and Liabilities in Point of Delivery, correct?
Hello, is there update on this?

Hello, I just discussed your question with our BA. The data in these two columns (“Liabilities in Billing Group” and “Liabilities in Point of Delivery”) is not correct for this case. We will discuss with the business what exactly should be displayed there.
In any case, you have the contracts extracted, so you should just find the one where the POD was last active.

Could you please clarify what you mean by “is not correct”? Do you mean that the logic behind it is not correct in general, or that there is a bug in this particular case? for the change part, i wrote description based on our discussion.
It is the exact logic of displaying liabilities in this columns.
